forecast-period.text: A low pressure system and trough currently over the eastern SA will gradually drift eastwards, clearing the border in the afternoon. A weak ridge of high pressure will develop south of the Bight on Wednesday, lingering into Thursday. A trough will then begin to move into the far west late Thursday, slowly drifting northeastwards across the state Friday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible light isolated showers and thunderstorms bringing little to no rainfall in the east during the morning, mostly clearing in the afternoon. Showers and storms developing over the north later in the day. Maximum temperatures above average in the east, grading to below average in the west. Moderate to fresh northeast to northwesterly winds about eastern parts at first, with fresh southwest to southeasterly winds in the west, extending throughout during the day.

Possible isolated late showers about windward coasts and the Mount Lofty Ranges. Isolated showers or thunderstorms developing in the far north and northwest. Maximum temperatures above average in the northeast, grading to below average elsewhere. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times near the coast.

Showers or thunderstorms about the far west and far north. Maximum temperatures generally above average, grading to below average about the southern agricultural area and in the northwest. Southeast to northeasterly winds, tending northwesterly in the far northwest during the evening.

text.p: Scattered showers across the north and west, extending into central and eastern parts in the afternoon but becoming more isolated. Thunderstorms across the north and west, possibly reaching the peninsulas during the day. Maximum temperatures mostly above average. East to southeasterly winds across the south and east, tending west to northwesterly across the north at times.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: Broadly less than 2 mm across the state. Falls increasing to 2 to 5 mm about the west, north and parts of the agricultural area, with isolated higher falls of 10 to 20 mm in the far northwest. Localised totals 15 to 25 mm with thunderstorms, increasing up to 35 mm in the far northwest.
